summary: A 1976 list of assigned network numbers for the ARPANET and connected networks. It is a registry-style document and is historic.

eli5.summary: This is a phone book listing which numbers were given to which networks, long before today's addresses.

subtitle: A 1976 registry of network numbers for early ARPANET experiments.

tldr.problem: Early ARPANET experiments needed a standard way to identify and reach different networks in inter-network communication.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC assigns unique decimal numbers to each network (like a phone area code) and specifies how network and host addresses fit into packet headers.
tldr.outcome: The numbering scheme was a prototype for later address assignments. RFC 717 is now historic, replaced by modern network addressing.

today: RFC 717 is Historic and has been superseded by modern IPv4 and IPv6 addressing schemes. It is preserved as a reference to early ARPANET architecture.

sections.title: Network Number Registry
sections.content: RFC 717 assigns identifying numbers to networks participating in early ARPANET inter-network protocol experiments. The assignment authority was Jon Postel at SRI-ARC. Four networks are listed: BBNRCCnet (3), SanFranPRnet (7), ARPANET (10), and BostonPRnet (11). These numbers served to uniquely identify each network in the experimental internet.
sections.eli5: Networks needed numbers just like houses need addresses. This document gave out numbers to different research networks.

sections.title: Network and Host Addressing
sections.content: The Internetwork header format used 8 bits for the destination network and 24 bits for the destination host address, with the same structure for source addresses. This meant a maximum of 256 networks could be identified and 16 million hosts per network. The total header overhead for routing information was 8 octets.
sections.eli5: Each address had two parts: which network, and which computer on that network.

sections.title: Protocol Header Structure
sections.content: The header included a Format field in bits 0-3 that identified which protocol was being used, allowing the packet to be routed to the correct protocol handler. Protocol values were defined as 1 for TCP, 2 for Secure TCP, and 17 for Cross Internet Debugging. The TCP-specific portion included sequence numbers, window size, control flags, and port numbers for application identification.
sections.eli5: The header told routers which protocol to use (like choosing between email or chat), and included sending/receiving ports.
